title: Indoor footwear: slippers, frailty and arthritis (UK)
meta_title: Indoor footwear: slippers, frailty and arthritis (UK)
meta_description: How to choose safer indoor footwear and slippers when you have arthritis and frailty, what to avoid, and when to ask for podiatry or footwear advice.

direct_answer: Worn, loose or backless slippers and walking in socks can increase the risk of falls. Safer indoor footwear has a fastening, a closed back, a firm heel, a thin grippy sole and enough room for painful toes. A podiatrist can advise if feet are swollen or misshapen.

content:
Many people spend most of the day indoors in slippers. With arthritis and frailty, what you wear on your feet at home can affect comfort and balance.

This guide explains what to look for in indoor footwear. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What to avoid

  • Backless or loose slippers.
  • Slippers that are worn, stretched or have smooth soles.
  • Walking in socks or tights on hard floors.
  • Thick, soft soles that make you less stable.

What to look for

  • A closed heel and fastening, such as Velcro.
  • A firm heel counter and a low, wide heel.
  • A thin, flexible, slip-resistant sole.
  • A wide, deep toe box for bunions or swelling.
  • Easy fastenings for painful hands.

If your feet are swollen or painful

Adjustable fastenings help when swelling changes during the day. Ask your GP about podiatry if you cannot find anything that fits. Ask your GP about new or unexplained swelling.

Other tips

Replace slippers when worn. A long-handled shoe horn can help. Keep a pair by the bed for night-time.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Are slippers dangerous?

Ill-fitting slippers can increase falls risk. Well-fitting, fastened slippers are safer.

Should I wear outdoor shoes indoors?

Some people find well-fitting shoes more stable. Choose what fits securely and feels steady.
